recipes.name: Acorn Candy Cookies
ingredients_raw: 24 milk chocolate candy kisses (such as Hershey's Kisses®), unwrapped
24 mini vanilla wafer cookies (such as Nilla®)

steps.text: Smear a small amount of frosting onto flat bottom of 1 candy kiss; press onto flat bottom of 1 vanilla wafer cookie. Smear a small amount of frosting onto flat bottom of 1 butterscotch chip; press onto rounded top of same cookie. Repeat with remaining frosting, candy kisses, wafer cookies, and butterscotch chips. Set aside to dry, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Acorn Candy Cookies
raw_recipe.description: This acorn candy cookies recipe is made with chocolate kisses, butterscotch chips, and vanilla wafer cookies. The cute cookies resemble little acorns.

video.description: These no-bake cookies are adorable and easy to make. Simply attach candy kisses to vanilla wafer cookies with chocolate frosting for the cutest acorn cookies. Everyone will love this kid-friendly recipe. Who doesn’t enjoy a simple chocolate dessert?

review.reviewBody: Too cute! These are so simple, and leave you kicking yourself saying, "Why didn't I think of these"? I guess that's why it's just such an ingenious little recipe! The best part is eating the ones you don't need for decorating! These are great to put out in candy dishes too. Thanks for yet another great recipe, What's for dinner, mom?

These are easy, and very good. I like butterscotch so I melted about 1/4 cup of butterscotch and used this to attach everything. Very easy to turn nilla wafers upside down. Dip bottom of kiss into melted chips and put on wafer. Let set about 3 minutes. Turn over and dip bottom of butterscotch chip into melted chips and put on top of wafer. Let set about 3 minutes. This makes them quit durable and you can even store them in zip lock bag for several days. If you don't like much butterscotch, you can melt chocolate chips (or any flavor) instead.

I made these and they were a hit. Very cute. I used cupcake frosting in the tube to "glue" the pieces together. WORKS really good! Peanut butter (as someone suggested) and regular frosting does not hold because it doesn't dry.
Next time I'll put a piece of walnut on the top instead of the butterscotch morsel. I think it will look better.
I also used the mini Nilla Waffers instead of the original size.

SO easy to make. I did make a few changes; 1) I used peanut butter chips instead of butterscotch. It was a much better flavor., and 2) instead of plain chocolate frosting (which can get super dry or super melty and thus the whole thing falls apart), I used royal icing (the tube kind that you can find in the grocery store). Just a small dab on each component and they held together very nicely (and didn't detract from the flavor).

Easy-peasy, tasty and adorable.

This is a fun recipe for the autumn season. I make it with the following changes: Use Nutter Butter minis instead of vanilla wafers, peanut butter chips in place of butterscotch, and then use peanut butter for the "glue". They look more like acorns and who doesn't love chocolate and peanut butter?! Thanks for the recipe!

YUMMY! I used Nutter Butter Bites in place of vanilla wafer cookies and Reese's Peanut Butter Chips in place of the butterscotch chips. To attach I melted some of each candy and dipped into it so it wouldn't show where it was attached. They were YUMMY! My reason for the change is that I was looking for something peanut butter for my step-father. This recipe is going to make him so happy. The hardest part is keeping Hubby away from them. I know I have to make more! Thanks WFDM for another YUMMY recipe!

***To those who do not agree with the butterscotch chip on the top - I used that due to ALLERGY issues. I never make peanut butter ANYTHING when giving food to anyone so I used the butterscotch. Please use whatever flavor you like*** I recommend that if you are using these for cupcake decorations to put them on just prior to serving as the cookie will absorb the moisture from the frosting and become soft. Also, I have found NutterButter Mini cookies that are perfect for these! The tops look textured like an acorn. These are fun and easy for kids to make!

So cute and so simple to make for a Halloween treat or anytime during the Fall season through Thanksgiving. I did use peanut butter chips in place of Butterscotch mainly for the reason that I already had them on hand, but also because they are less sweet than Butterscotch. Of course, peanut butter and chocolate do go so nicely together.

Literally so cute and easy! I substituted chocolate icing for Nutella and butterscotch chips to milk chocolate and peanut butter and loveeeedd the combination. Hopefully everyone at my work party tomorrow agrees!

Needed something to take up to the hospital as a thank you to all the nurses caring for my mom. These were perfect and so easy. I did substitute chocolate PB2 (if you've never tried it, it's fabulous!!) peanut butter powder for the prepared icing and used peanut butter chips since that's all my store had at the time. The PB2 made it so easy to attach the kisses - I mixed it a little thicker than I would for normal peanut butter. So much fun to prepare!

These are SOOOOOOO fun! I made them using the almond filled kisses, mini Nutter Butter sandwich cookies (pulled apart) and mini chocolate chips. The kids really liked the design on the Nutter Butters and the chocolate/peanut butter taste!
Great time to do with family and have some fun! Everyone enjoyed them!
Made these with 6,5,&4 year old kids for Thanksgiving treat. We had a blast making these tasty treats.

These are so easy and delicious! I used peanut butter instead of melted chocolate to reduce the sweetness and to add protein. I also used Reeses chips instead of butterscotch. The peanut butter doesn't hold a well but they did fine sitting on a plate.
These were super easy to do and tasted great. The perfect snack!

This was a great and simple recipe, one that kids can easily participate in (although parents might want to put the butterscotch chips on since they are very tiny). I brought them to Thanksgiving dinner at my Amish friend's house and everyone loved them, not only for their taste but because they were simply too cute! If you can make Amish cooks rave over something, you know it's a keeper...
Just finished making these on the Friday after Thanksgiving with my 4 yo grand-daughter. We loved making these together and she loved eating the ingredients! PS. They are actually tasty too!!
Super cute and the kids loved making them.
This was so good! The kids love it, and they can make it completely by themselves!!! Definitely will make again!!!!
